xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Union of India & ANR (Central Board of Excise & Customs)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The disputed matter is on account of Charges of Additional duty of customs (CVD) on Import of Tyre Scrap during the period covered from April 01, 2013 to June 30, 2017. Earlier Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed order dt 03.05.2017 in our favour of Company but department filed Appeal at Hon'ble Supreme Court on 23 July 2018, Supreme Court Remanded back the matter for Fresh Adjudication to Hon'ble igh Court of Delhi. Amount of dispute is not specified Not specifed Hon'ble High Court of Delhi to decide on Law (amount involved Rs. 356.42 Lakhs). The Case is under adjudication with Hon'ble High Court of Delhi
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Commissioner of GST and Central Excise (Appeals II), Chennai
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The disputed matter is on account of Credit of CVD on tyre scrap during the period covered from April 01, 2013 to June 30, 2017, after high court order dt 03.05.2017, and after the Appeal Order Dt 30.07.2024 which upheld against the Company where as per Department Refund should be claimed, and credit of Special Additional duty (SAD) (amount involved is Rs. 153.38 lakh). The case of yet to be listed for hearing at Customs, Excise And Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Chennai
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Government of India /Ministry of finance Office of the Commissioner of Goods & Services Tax, GST Bhawan CGO complex, NH IV, Faridabad-121 001
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: Denail of GST Input Tax Credit Rs. 261.42 Lakhs relating to FY 2020-21 & 2021-22 on Purchase of Goods Traded. Appeal to be filed with Commissioner (Appeals) Gurugram
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Court of the District Revenue Officer-cum-Land Acquisition Collector, Panipat, Haryana
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: Petition under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act before the Court of the District Revenue Officer-cum-Land Acquisition Collector, Panipat, for compensation of approximately Rs. 663.20 lakhs along with all the statutory benefits has been sought by our Company, with respect to land not in our possession, by way of the Petition. Additionally, we have claimed a compensation of Rs. 7,500.00 lakhs on the grounds of construction costs and loss of profits likely to be caused due to the acquisition of land, which may or may not be awarded to our Company.
